solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Voice raised after care of part of horse's foot

indicators.note: the reversed voice comes after the care-of letters in the answer

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a tenor is a singing voice

explanation.surface: A singer's voice lifted after the vet has tended a horse's hoof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns TENOR upwards in this down entry to give RONET.
explanation.definitionFit: The coronet is the band of soft tissue just above the hoof on a horse's leg.

clue.text: Entwined thread etc moved by progressive degrees

indicators.note: things entwined are twisted together, so the letters of these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Twisted thread and similar stuff wound along a notch at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entwined' scrambles THREAD ETC into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ratchet is to move step by step, like a ratchet wheel clicking forward one tooth at a time.

clue.text: Old acts and droit without limits for city toll

indicators.note: losing their limits, both words shed their first and last letters, leaving only the inside

explanation.surface: Ancient statutes and legal rights, stripped back, behind a charge for entering a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without limits' trims ACTS to CT and DROIT to ROI.
explanation.definitionFit: An octroi was a duty levied on goods brought into a town, especially in France.

clue.text: Scaremonger's weapon in atomic schedule

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for atomic, as in A-bomb

indicators.note: the weapon sits in the schedule, splitting it open

parts.note: a list is a schedule of items
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A fear-spreader's arsenal is written into a nuclear plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the containment signal; 'atomic' gives just A, as in A-bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarmist needlessly spreads fear, which is what a scaremonger does.

clue.text: Contrary to natural feelings, disliking the start of gentle showery weather

parts.note: to be against something is to dislike it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only the opening of gentle is taken

parts.note: rain is showery weather

explanation.surface: Someone who hates the beginning of a soft drizzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes G from 'gentle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Going against the grain is an idiom for acting contrary to one's natural inclination.

clue.text: Opening digits America's used with most of communication lines?

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: to reach someone is to get in touch, so reach is communication
an ode is a few lines of poetry

explanation.surface: An American practice of combining much of a message with telephone wires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' takes the H off REACH; ''s used with' only links the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: An area code is the set of digits dialled at the start of a phone number for a region.

clue.text: Bungle military intelligence's event

parts.note: MI is military intelligence, with the 's giving MIS
a do is a party or event

explanation.surface: The spy agency botches an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdo is to do something badly, which is what bungling is.

clue.text: Safekeeping of gold in field of action

indicators.note: the gold sits inside the field of action

parts.note: a stage is a scene or field of action
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Keeping gold secure on a battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold comes from heraldry, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is the keeping of things in a safe place, so safekeeping.

clue.text: Fitting together of disparate elements associated with lawgiver

definitions.meaning: a whole made of many different pieces fitted together
... also means relating to Moses, the biblical lawgiver

explanation.surface: Assembling mismatched parts, linked to someone who made laws.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a picture of assembled fragments; the adjective describes things relating to Moses, who received the Ten Commandments.

clue.text: Dislike American translation

parts.note: a version is a rendering or translation of a text

explanation.surface: Not liking how an American translated something.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong feeling of dislike for something.

clue.text: Interest cut short before it returned for compositions

indicators.note: the shortened interest comes before the turned-round word
cutting a word short drops its final letter

parts.note: a concern is an interest or matter one cares about

indicators.note: returned means the little word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: Losing interest just before something comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the N from CONCERN, and 'returned' makes IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerti are musical works for soloist and orchestra, the Italian plural of concerto.

clue.text: Novel carol initially heard sung by choir

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are made into a new arrangement
initially means only the first letter of heard is used

explanation.surface: A new Christmas carol first performed by singers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes H from 'heard'; 'Novel' then mixes CAROL with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music written for or performed by a choir.

clue.text: Calamitous stage direction not potentially adroit for development

indicators.note: a calamitous outcome is a disaster, so the letters of stage direction are jumbled; not potentially then removes the letters of adroit

explanation.surface: A disastrous stage direction, hardly a skilful one, for a new production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calamitous' scrambles STAGE DIRECTION; 'not potentially adroit' takes out ADROIT's letters, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetics studies how inherited traits shape the growth of living things, the setter's loose sense of development.

clue.text: Stories about regularly adept or developing little swimmers

indicators.note: the stories go about, around, the picked letters

parts.note: tales are stories

indicators.note: taking letters regularly means every other one, here the second, fourth and sixth of adept or

explanation.surface: Tales of a competent person, or one still learning, featuring small swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'adept or', and 'about' wraps the stories round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tadpoles are frog larvae, small aquatic creatures that grow into frogs.

clue.text: Wrongdoers cease interrupting proposals

indicators.note: one word interrupting another breaks into it, so it goes inside

parts.note: offers are proposals
to end is to cease

explanation.surface: Criminals halt the proposals mid-flow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' signals one word breaking into the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Offenders are people who break the law, so wrongdoers.

clue.text: Person with honour, one that's in forever, possessing go

indicators.note: the lifer possessing the go holds it inside

parts.note: a lifer is a prisoner serving a life sentence, in jail for good
go is slang for pee, to urinate

explanation.surface: An honoured figure, a permanent fixture, full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possessing' signals containment. A life peer sits in Britain's House of Lords for life but cannot pass the title on.
explanation.definitionFit: A life peer is someone given a non-hereditary peerage, a high honour in Britain.

clue.text: Abrasive hag reportedly offering snack for compulsive gambler?

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are as heard when said, not as written

parts.note: sand is an abrasive, used for scouring; a witch is a hag

explanation.surface: A harsh old woman supposedly serving food to a gambling addict.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earl of Sandwich reputedly had meat put between bread so he need not leave the gaming table; hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich is a snack, named after an earl said to be a compulsive gambler.

clue.text: Electrical device suitable in construction of road

indicators.note: the suitable word goes in the rearranged road
a construction of something builds it anew, so the letters of road are rearranged

parts.note: apt means suitable

explanation.surface: A fitting gadget used in roadbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'construction of' rearranges the road to ADOR, and 'in' puts the suitable word inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor is a fitting that lets one plug or device connect to a differently shaped socket.

clue.text: Classical man academically pens annual publication

indicators.note: pens here means encloses, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A scholar of the classics writes a yearly book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means enclosing: the answer is inside 'ClassicAL MAN ACademically'.
explanation.definitionFit: An almanac is a calendar book issued every year with dates, tides and other data.

clue.text: Make weak reactionary moan separating English wines, essentially, from the French

indicators.note: the reversed moan separates the first pair of pieces from the last one
essentially means the core, the middle letter of wines
reactionary means going back, so the moan is read backwards

parts.note: beef is slang for a complaint, a moan
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A backward-looking complaint keeps the English and French wine trade apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reactionary' turns the moan round to FEEB; 'essentially' takes the middle of 'wines'; 'separating' sets the moan between the English pair and the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfeeble is to weaken, sapping someone's strength.

clue.text: With little to spare concealing morning's dearth

indicators.note: concealing means the fine word hides the morning inside it

parts.note: cutting it fine leaves little to spare, so fine
AM is morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Hiding a morning shortage when supplies are tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With little to spare' is the idiom cutting it fine; 'concealing' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A famine is an extreme shortage of food, and dearth means scarcity.

clue.text: Promise dad part in play

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad
a role is an actor's part in a play

explanation.surface: A father vows to take a role in a stage production.
explanation.definitionFit: Parole originally means a word of honour, a prisoner's pledge given on release.

clue.text: Theatre masonry styles

definitions.meaning: a dramatic art form, a branch of theatre
the plural of opus, a style of Roman masonry such as opus reticulatum

explanation.surface: A playhouse's patterns of stonework.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is staged musical drama; Roman builders named their wall-facing techniques opus, plural opera.

clue.text: With intention of improving, including the setter, attempt further contact

indicators.note: the redial word includes the setter, holding it inside

parts.note: to redial is to try a phone number again
the setter refers to herself as me

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler tries calling again, hoping to make things better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the setter' is the compiler speaking of herself; 'including' signals containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Remedial describes something meant to correct or improve a fault, as in remedial lessons.

clue.text: This appears briefly in 2 and so forth

definitions.meaning: the abbreviated form, etc, appears in the clue to 2 Down, Entwined thread etc
the Latin phrase means and the rest, so and so forth

explanation.surface: Something shown in shortened form in another clue, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2 Down clue reads 'Entwined thread etc', and etc is the short form of this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for and the rest, used to mean and so on.

clue.text: Typical old European endlessly on line

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a Norman was one of the medieval people of Normandy

explanation.surface: An ancient continental always standing in a queue is the usual sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the final N from NORMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means usual or standard, so typical.

clue.text: Hearing unit of scoring in cricket test

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
runs are how batsmen score in cricket

explanation.surface: A court case and a single run make a cricket test match.
explanation.walkthrough: A run is one point scored by batters running between the wickets in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a test of something before it is used for real.
